pickFarmDesc: Pick a farm, manage its field boundaries, and inspect versions and areas.
noFarmsDesc: A farm is the container for fields and their boundaries. Create your first one — it takes 20 seconds.
loadFarmsError: Could not load farms. Please retry.
loadFieldsError: Could not load fields — try again.
noFieldsYetTitle: No fields in this farm yet
noFieldsDesc: Add a field with a GeoJSON boundary — use the example square if you just want to try it out.
selectFarmHint: Select a farm on the left to see its fields.
selectFieldHint: Select a field above to see its offline map, geodesic area, boundary versions and actions.
geometryHint: Paste a GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon (EPSG:4326 lon/lat). The backend repairs and validates it with PostGIS; areas are geodesic WGS84.
geometryRepaired: The backend repaired the geometry before storing it.
createDesc: A farm groups fields and sets the geographic + currency context for decisions.
countryHint: 2 letters, e.g. EG, IT, US, TH.
countryRequired: Country must be exactly 2 letters (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).
languageRequired: Preferred language must be a 2-letter code.
addFieldDesc: The boundary is validated by PostGIS. If something is off (self-intersections, unclosed rings), the response tells you exactly what was fixed.
fieldNameRequired: Give the field a name first.
fieldCreatedWarnings: Field created — but review the geometry warnings
warningsFromPostgis: {count, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}} from PostGIS validation.
adjustGeometryRetry: Adjust the geometry and try again.
renameDesc: Boundaries and observations keep their history — only the label changes.
updateBoundaryDesc: Boundary history is never overwritten: every change is stored as a new version with its recomputed area.
mapWillRefresh: The map and version list will refresh automatically.
mapUnavailable: Map payload unavailable — the boundary is still stored safely.
technicalNote: Technical detail: areas come from PostGIS geodesic computation (WGS84 ellipsoid). The map above is an offline preview — north is up, scale in metric units.
